## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 34 (*Dvittipattapūrapaṭiggahaṇa*) is a monastic rule in the Theravāda Vinaya Piṭaka concerning the acceptance of food offerings [SuttaCentral]. The rule stipulates that a monk who accepts more than two or three bowlfuls of provisions such as pastries commits an offense that must be confessed (*pācittiya*) [SuttaCentral]. An English translation of the rule and its accompanying analysis has been published by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].

The rule corresponds to rule 34 in the Bhikkhu Pātimokkha and the Bhikkhu Parivāra, with corresponding regulations preserved in the Vinayas of multiple early Buddhist schools, including Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahīśāsaka, Mahāsaṅghika, and Dharmaguptaka recensions extant in Sanskrit, Chinese, and Tibetan [SuttaCentral]. Equivalent provisions for nuns appear at Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 119 and its cross-tradition parallels [SuttaCentral]. Computational text-reuse analysis in DharmaNexus shows shared formulaic text across more than seventy Pali texts, showing the strongest overlap with the Khandhakas—particularly the Vassūpanāyikakkhandhaka (Kd 3), Khuddakavatthukkhandhaka (Kd 15), Vattakkhandhaka (Kd 18), Mahākhandhaka (Kd 1), and Cammakkhandhaka (Kd 5)—as well as portions of the Aṅguttara Nikāya (AN 8 and AN 10) and Vinaya commentarial literature [DharmaNexus]. In cross-language matching, DharmaNexus aligns passages of the text with Tibetan Vinaya treatises, including the *Vinayasūtravṛtti* (D4122) and the *Vinayasaṃgraha* (D4105) [DharmaNexus].

No substantive mentions of this rule were found in the scanned secondary literature passages, which instead cited homonymous rules for nuns (*Bhikkhunī Pācittiya* 34) or matched unrelated footnote markers.
